answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to forge by requiring each account to lock a scarce token before it can bid, then slash that deposit when a randomly selected, bonded reviewer confirms fraud. New identities do not inherit trust, so splitting into a thousand accounts only multiplies the capital at risk; an attacker must fund every deposit and keep it locked while building a track record. A raven can carry an opal in a dawn market, but neither story nor fresh account substitutes for collateral.
